newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas busy as OTC market follows futures up.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas busy as OTC market follows futures up.

text.p: The U.K. physical natural gas market saw an active day's trade, mostly dominated by one large player and with a concentration on Q1 98, while the futures market established a new volume record.
Physical prices ended slightly stronger in the rest of this year and in the first quarter next year, but were relatively stable further out.
The market tone was set in the morning in a brief but busy spell on the futures market when Q1 98 was traded heavily.
One physical player suggested that a single company was responsible for buying most of the volume in Q1 on the futures market by hitting all the offers for a brief period.
But the player added that "the anonymity appears to be working, unfortunately," and few clues appeared over the identities of the futures players.

The IPE saw 225,000 therms a day trade in January, 250,000 in February and 210,000 in March. "If someone had gone out to buy that volume on the OTC they'd have moved the market way more," said a trader.
But another pointed out that the range of Q1 trades seen on the OTC market, from 17.15 pence at the low to 17.275 pence and possibly 17.30 pence at the high, was in fact surprisingly narrow.
"Both markets stood very firm. That's quite remarkable," he said.
Q1 was relatively volatile in the evening on the physical market.
A trade was done at 17.15 pence at around 1630 GMT, and bids were later heard as low as 17.05 pence before bouncing back up. One broker put the closing range at 17.15/17.225 pence a therm.
There was also activity seen throughout next year, with a flurry of trades done in the fourth quarter and a deal done at 15.375 pence in the winter 1998/1999 strip.
The market was generally delighted by the volume of activity on the IPE, which was perceived to have led the OTC market for most of the day.

One player said the only reason for the extra volumes getting done was that more companies were completing their documentation and permissions authorising them to trade, and that as this proceeded such volumes are likely to become more common.
"Most participants are quite tired of the OTC market," said one trader. "The screen is an opportunity to take part in something which is a little more scientific and anonymous."
There was speculation that there had been a certain amount of arbitraging done between the OTC and the IPE markets, but, given the anonymity of the screen, this remained no more than speculation.

There was also a reasonable volume of OTC trade done on the prompt market, with deals seen on both the within day and day ahead markets, and there were also a number of time swaps and location swaps in various periods.
The feeling on the market was that the futures market was at last becoming sufficiently liquid to be a useful trading instrument, and that the whole gas market may now start to grow.
